prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universally “best” HVAC company — the right contractor depends on your home, budget, timing, and whether you want a local company or a national franchise. I can find highly rated contractors near you and recommend the top options if you tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s how to identify the best HVAC company to replace your air conditioner and what to ask them.

What I need from you to give specific recommendations
- ZIP code or neighborhood
- Home type and square footage (roughly)
- Budget or brand preference (e.g., Carrier/Trane/Lennox vs. value brands)
- Timeline (ASAP vs. can wait for bids)
- Any existing issues (ductwork problems, recent repairs, unit age)

If you want me to search now, give your ZIP and I’ll return a short list of 3–5 highly rated, trustworthy companies with links to reviews.

How to choose the best contractor (quick checklist)
- Proper credentials: licensed in Georgia (if applicable for your locality), EPA Section 608 certification for refrigerant handling, and current liability insurance.
- Technician qualifications: NATE-certified technicians are a good sign.
- Local reputation: 4+ star Google/Yelp ratings, positive recent reviews, and good BBB rating.
- Manufacturer relationships: factory-authorized dealer for the brand you want (helps with warranty).
- Written estimate: itemized quote listing equipment model, SEER rating, accessories, labor, permits, and total price.
- Sizing & design: they should perform or show a Manual J load calculation (not just “rule of thumb” sizing).
- Installation quality: matched coil and condenser, proper refrigerant charge, correct airflow, and quality duct sealing/insulation if needed.
- Warranties & labor guarantees: good equipment warranty plus a clear workmanship warranty; get terms in writing.
- Permits & code: contractor should pull local permits and arrange inspections if required.
- References & recent jobs: ask for local references or examples of recent installs.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are your technicians NATE-certified and EPA-608 certified?
- Can you provide an itemized written estimate and equipment specs (make/model, SEER)?
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation and show the results?
- Are you a factory-authorized dealer for this brand? What warranties are included?
- Who will pull the permit and handle inspections?
- How do you handle unexpected issues (e.g., duct repairs)? How are change orders priced?
- Can I see references for installs in my neighborhood in the last 6–12 months?
- What are payment, financing, and rebate options?

How to compare bids
- Don’t pick purely on lowest price. Compare equipment SEER, whether the system is matched, included labor warranty length, and scope of work (ductwork, thermostats, disconnects, pad, line-set, evacuation).
- Ask each contractor to explain long-term operating cost differences (SEER, variable-speed compressors, two-stage vs single-stage).

If you give your ZIP code I’ll:
- Pull up 3–5 well-rated, licensed HVAC companies near you,
- Summarize strengths, approximate price ranges, and review snapshots,
- Suggest which to call first based on your priorities (lowest price, highest workmanship, best warranty, fastest availability).

Which would you prefer — a quick local shortlist, or help preparing questions and a checklist you can use while calling contractors?
